newsitem.title: JAPAN: Two Osaka "shinkin" firms say to merge November 4.
newsitem.headline: Two Osaka "shinkin" firms say to merge November 4.

text.p: Two Osaka-based credit associations, Osaka City Shinkin Bank and Osaka Chuo Shinkin Bank, said on Tuesday that they would merge on November 4.

The merged entity, which will retain the name Osaka City Shinkin Bank, will hold deposits worth one trillion yen, making it the 17th biggest among the nation's 412 credit associations, the two credit associations said. Osaka Chuo Shinkin Bank will be dissolved upon the merger, they added.

Shinkin banks are small, locally based credit associations which take deposits and lend mainly to members and are supervised by the Ministry of Finance. Although going by the name shinkin banks, they are not classified as banks under Japanese law.
